Join hackathon Who can participate Ages 13 to 99 only Specific countries/territories excluded View full rules October 01 at 2:45am EDT to deadline View schedule Deadline: Sep 30, 2026 @ 11:45pm PDT Apple Google Outlook Online Public $ 740,000 in cash 23849 participants RevenueCat Design Gaming Mobile Welcome to the RevenueCat Shipaton — the mobile hackathon that's all about shipping… a ton. At RevenueCat, we're all about supporting developers to build and monetize amazing apps. After the overwhelming success of last year's Shipaton, we're thrilled to announce the return of our global hackathon — and this year, we're going bigger than ever. This August and September, we're inviting builders from all corners of the globe to ship new apps and compete for over $700,000 in cash prizes and truly unique rewards — over $1 million worth of prizes in total. The challenge Ship a brand-new app to the App Store, Google Play Store, or — new this year — the Samsung Galaxy Store, between August 1st and September 30th, 2026. Integrate the RevenueCat SDK to power at least one in-app purchase or serve ads through RevenueCat Ads. Our goal is to give you that final push to ship that project you've had in the back of your mind but never took the time to get started. Note: Updates to previously released apps won't qualify - it's all about bringing something new to life! You can brainstorm, build, and post before August 1st, but your app must be released for the first time during the Shipaton window. Bigger and better Last year's Shipaton blew us away. Hundreds of new apps launched, thousands of #BuildInPublic posts went out, communities from Tokyo to Seoul to London hosted Shipaton IRL events, and winning teams ended up on stage in New York, accepting their Shippy trophies with their apps lighting up a Times Square billboard. Inspired by your amazing contributions, we've upped the ante for 2026: Over $700,000 in cash prizes — and growing as more sponsors join. Winning apps featured on giant billboards in Times Square. Flights to New York City for the Shippies red carpet award ceremony and RevenueCat's App Growth Annual conference. Press coverage for winners on 9to5Mac and 9to5Google. NEW: Investor exposure through the Shipaton Growth Fund. Categories Grand Prize: Goes to the app that gains the most user traction and growth momentum during the event. We want to hear about what you've done post-release to push your app growth to the next level. [NEW] Next Gen Award: A student-only category for the best app submitted by active students — high school, university, bootcamp, campus dev club, anyone learning the craft. Judged on a video submission and open-source code, so no paid Apple or Google developer account is required. Open to students 13 and up. If you're under the age of majority where you live, a parent or guardian just needs to consent and agree to the rules on your behalf. Learn more on the Next Gen page . [NEW] Catvertising Award: Celebrates the most creative and effective use of RevenueCat Ads as a monetization method. We're looking for clever placements, smart integration with the rest of the revenue stack, and an experience users don't hate. [NEW] Best Game Award: For the best mobile game shipped during the event. We're looking for great gameplay, art direction, and a monetization fit that suits the genre. #BuildInPublic Award: For developers who share the most interesting development journey on social media. We're looking for compelling lessons learned or clever ideas that came from engaging with the community. HAMM Award (Help Apps Make Money): RevenueCat exists to "Help Apps Make More Money". This award goes to the project that designs the most robust and creative monetization strategy. RevenueCat Design Award: For the app that best represents the craft of app development — regardless of business potential. We're looking for innovative ideas and/or beautiful app design and animations. RevenueCat Peace Prize: Awarded to the project that provides the greatest social good. We're looking for apps with big benefits to communities or society at large. Conflict of Interest Award: A special category for RevenueCat employees and sponsors who couldn't resist joining the fun. No cash prizes, but a shot at glory. Influencer Award — Productivity: Christopher Lawley For a polished productivity app that gives Apple power users one fast, focused place to save and retrieve reusable text snippets, documents, files, and images. Judges will consider product focus, speed, organization, intelligent features, and the quality of the overall design. Influencer Award — Nutrition & Healthy Eating: Abbey’s Kitchen For a flexible nutrition app inspired by Abbey’s Hunger Crushing Combo framework. Judges are looking for a compassionate, practical experience that helps users create more satisfying meals in real-life situations without calorie counting, macro tracking, or restrictive meal plans. Influencer Award — Yoga & Fitness: Simone Sharice For a personalized wellness companion that answers, “What should I do today?” Judges will consider how effectively the app turns movement, Pilates, recovery, and other wellness needs into a clear, achievable daily plan without creating more information overload. Influencer Award — Career Coaching: Leadership Heather For an app that helps new managers practise difficult workplace conversations before the stakes are real. Judges are looking for realistic scenarios, useful feedback, confidence-building experiences, and active practice with situations such as feedback, boundaries, and saying no. Influencer Award — Gaming: Mr Lewis Blogs Gaming For a gaming bucket-list app that makes it easy to save games at the moment of discovery. Judges will consider how effectively users can organize, complete, rate, and share games, along with whether managing a backlog feels enjoyable rather than like another chore. Ship Kotlin Everywhere — JetBrains Recognizes a creative, polished app built for both iOS and Android using Kotlin Multiplatform, Compose Multiplatform, or both. Judges will consider cross-platform quality, consistency, and effective use of Kotlin. Optional consideration may be given to useful build content and contributions to the Kotlin Multiplatform community. Most Viral App — Noise Awarded to the app that captures the most attention in its market through high-quality, scalable content that converts into downloads. Judges will consider virality, whether the creative formats can be repeated at scale, and how clearly the content communicates the app’s value and addresses users’ needs. Best App for Galaxy — Samsung Recognizes a high-quality app published on the Galaxy Store and thoughtfully optimized for Samsung Galaxy users. Judges will consider the overall app experience and Galaxy-specific optimization, including foldable-device support, Samsung features, and device performance. Galaxy Store exclusivity may receive bonus consideration but is not required. Replit’s Idea to Income Recognizes a project that uses Replit to turn a new idea into a live, monetizing mobile app. Judges will primarily consider consistent week-over-week growth in revenue and transactions, supported by paying-user traction, product craft, visual design, and meaningful community engagement. Keep Them Coming Back Award — OneSignal Recognizes an app that uses OneSignal thoughtfully to bring users back. Judges will consider the quality and stability of the implementation, the value it adds to the user experience, and how creatively the app uses campaigns, push notifications, Journeys, or advanced messaging capabilities. The Growth Loop Award — Layers Recognizes a team that treats growth as a process of testing, measuring, learning, and improving. Judges will consider the clarity of the audience and growth hypothesis, how Layers was used to run and observe a focused experiment, whether the SDK was installed correctly, and what the team learned or would try next. Funnel Vision Award — Stripe Recognizes a project that launches a web funnel using RevenueCat Funnels and Stripe. Judges will consider the qualifying web payment volume processed during the measurement period and whether the funnel is thoughtfully designed, functional, and effectively implemented. Prize structure You can find the official details of prizes at the bottom of this page, but here's how it all breaks down: Grand Prize Winner $100,000 Trip to New York City for the Shippies award ceremony and RevenueCat's App Growth Annual conference Custom Shippy trophy (presented live on stage!) App featured on a massive Times Square billboard Media spotlight on 9to5Mac and 9to5Google #BuildInPublic Category 1st Place: $30,000 + custom Shippy trophy + Times Square billboard feature + media spotlight + Trip to New York City for the Shippies award ceremony and RevenueCat's App Growth Annual conference 2nd Place: $20,000 3rd Place: $10,000 OneSignal's Keep Them Coming Back Award winner 1st Place: $25,000 + custom Shippy trophy + Times Square billboard feature + media spotlight 2nd Place: $15,000 3rd Place: $5,000 All Other Categories 1st Place: $20,000 + custom Shippy trophy + Times Square billboard feature + media spotlight 2nd Place: $10,000 3rd Place: $5,000 Supported by the industry This year, our sponsors have shown up big. Huge thanks to Replit, OneSignal, JetBrains, Layers, Noise, Stripe, and Samsung for coming in as category sponsors for Shipaton 2026. And more sponsors are joining the fun all the time, which means bigger cash prizes and more additions to the Ship Kit. Ship Kit is back: Freebies for every Shipaton participant Ship Kit is your bundle of tools, credits, deals, and resources from our sponsors to help you build faster, launch better, and save a lot of money along the way. Some deals are while supplies last, so the sooner you register at the top of this page, the sooner you get access as Ship Kit starts to roll out. The #ShipatonSale If you have an app, tool, service, course, or template that could help Shipaton builders, run a sale for participants and share it with the #ShipatonSale hashtag. Submit it on the Shipaton website and we'll list community sales for everyone to find. Even if you're not competing, there are ways to support the builders who are. Shipaton IRL: Events near you We're excited to take Shipaton directly to developers around the world with Shipaton IRL. Last year, builders gathered in Tokyo, Seoul, London, St. Louis, Barcelona, Delhi, Vancouver, Warsaw, Skopje, and dozens of cities in between. This year, we want even more: kickoff parties, co-working days, weekend build sprints, launch-day meetups, and campus hackathons. Check out the events page regularly, as new events are being added all the time! Want to host a Shipaton event yourself? Apply now - we'd love to support you. Approved hosts get a Meetup-in-a-box with Shipaton swag, food vouchers, and organizer resources, and we'll promote your event to the massive Shipaton audience. Perfect for developer communities, hacker clubs, and student organizers planning campus events. Join the conversation on Discord! Shipaton isn't just about shipping code - it's about community. Whether you're brainstorming your first idea or prepping for launch day, the official Shipaton Discord is the place to connect, collaborate, and share the journey. Inside, you'll find fellow builders from around the world debugging code, running paywall experiments, discussing launch strategies, and more. Looking to form a team? Need quick feedback? Want to hang out with other shippers? You'll find it here. We've also created a dedicated #post-engagement-boost channel where you can share your YouTube videos, posts, and other #BuildInPublic content so other participants can like, comment, or share to help you reach a bigger audience. It's all about creating a positive, encouraging space where we lift each other - and help each other ship. Shipaton Livestreams Throughout the event, we'll host twice-a-week livestreams with expert guests, practical sessions, and live Q&A — so you're never building alone for two months. Come say hi 👋 and make the most of Shipaton! Ready, set, ship! Submissions open on August 1st and close on September 30th. Be sure to carefully review all submission requirements to ensure your app qualifies. We're beyond excited to see what the global builder community creates this year. Register today, and we'll keep you updated via the email address you use there. Let's get shipping! Requirements WHAT TO BUILD Entrants must create a working software application that uses the RevenueCat SDK to power at least one in-app or web purchase (each a "Project"). Apps must be built for iOS, iPadOS, macOS, or Android. The first public version of your app must be released between August 1 and September 30, 2026 . Students competing for the Next Gen Award follow a different, lower-friction path: submit a video and source code instead of a published store listing. No paid Apple or Google developer account required. Students under the age of majority where they reside may enter the Next Gen Award (minimum age 13) with parent or guardian consent. See Section 3 of the official rules. What to submit on Devpost Every submission must include: A text description of your app's features and functionality. A demo video of your project. The video: Should show the app running on the device it was built for. Must be no longer than 2 minutes of essential footage — judges are not required to watch beyond two minutes. Must be uploaded to and publicly visible on YouTube or Vimeo, with the link provided on this form. Must not include third-party trademarks or copyrighted music/material unless you have permission to use it. A URL to your fully published app on the App Store or Google Play or Samsung Galaxy Store. A 1024×1024 app icon . At least one screenshot of the app at 1179px × 2556px with no device frame . Either a free trial in your app, or a promo code so judges can unlock the in-app purchase and test all premium features. Join hackathon Who can participate Ages 13 to 99 only Specific countries/territories excluded View full rules October 01 at 2:45am EDT to deadline View schedule Deadline: Sep 30, 2026 @ 11:45pm PDT Apple Google Outlook Online Public $ 740,000 in cash 23849 participants RevenueCat Design Gaming Mobile Welcome to the RevenueCat Shipaton — the mobile hackathon that's all about shipping… a ton. At RevenueCat, we're all about supporting developers to build and monetize amazing apps. After the overwhelming success of last year's Shipaton, we're thrilled to announce the return of our global hackathon — and this year, we're going bigger than ever. This August and September, we're inviting builders from all corners of the globe to ship new apps and compete for over $700,000 in cash prizes and truly unique rewards — over $1 million worth of prizes in total. The challenge Ship a brand-new app to the App Store, Google Play Store, or — new this year — the Samsung Galaxy Store, between August 1st and September 30th, 2026. Integrate the RevenueCat SDK to power at least one in-app purchase or serve ads through RevenueCat Ads. Our goal is to give you that final push to ship that project you've had in the back of your mind but never took the time to get started. Note: Updates to previously released apps won't qualify - it's all about bringing something new to life! You can brainstorm, build, and post before August 1st, but your app must be released for the first time during the Shipaton window. Bigger and better Last year's Shipaton blew us away. Hundreds of new apps launched, thousands of #BuildInPublic posts went out, communities from Tokyo to Seoul to London hosted Shipaton IRL events, and winning teams ended up on stage in New York, accepting their Shippy trophies with their apps lighting up a Times Square billboard. Inspired by your amazing contributions, we've upped the ante for 2026: Over $700,000 in cash prizes — and growing as more sponsors join. Winning apps featured on giant billboards in Times Square. Flights to New York City for the Shippies red carpet award ceremony and RevenueCat's App Growth Annual conference. Press coverage for winners on 9to5Mac and 9to5Google. NEW: Investor exposure through the Shipaton Growth Fund. Categories Grand Prize: Goes to the app that gains the most user traction and growth momentum during the event. We want to hear about what you've done post-release to push your app growth to the next level. [NEW] Next Gen Award: A student-only category for the best app submitted by active students — high school, university, bootcamp, campus dev club, anyone learning the craft. Judged on a video submission and open-source code, so no paid Apple or Google developer account is required. Open to students 13 and up. If you're under the age of majority where you live, a parent or guardian just needs to consent and agree to the rules on your behalf. Learn more on the Next Gen page . [NEW] Catvertising Award: Celebrates the most creative and effective use of RevenueCat Ads as a monetization method. We're looking for clever placements, smart integration with the rest of the revenue stack, and an experience users don't hate. [NEW] Best Game Award: For the best mobile game shipped during the event. We're looking for great gameplay, art direction, and a monetization fit that suits the genre. #BuildInPublic Award: For developers who share the most interesting development journey on social media. We're looking for compelling lessons learned or clever ideas that came from engaging with the community. HAMM Award (Help Apps Make Money): RevenueCat exists to "Help Apps Make More Money". This award goes to the project that designs the most robust and creative monetization strategy. RevenueCat Design Award: For the app that best represents the craft of app development — regardless of business potential. We're looking for innovative ideas and/or beautiful app design and animations. RevenueCat Peace Prize: Awarded to the project that provides the greatest social good. We're looking for apps with big benefits to communities or society at large. Conflict of Interest Award: A special category for RevenueCat employees and sponsors who couldn't resist joining the fun. No cash prizes, but a shot at glory. Influencer Award — Productivity: Christopher Lawley For a polished productivity app that gives Apple power users one fast, focused place to save and retrieve reusable text snippets, documents, files, and images. Judges will consider product focus, speed, organization, intelligent features, and the quality of the overall design. Influencer Award — Nutrition & Healthy Eating: Abbey’s Kitchen For a flexible nutrition app inspired by Abbey’s Hunger Crushing Combo framework. Judges are looking for a compassionate, practical experience that helps users create more satisfying meals in real-life situations without calorie counting, macro tracking, or restrictive meal plans. Influencer Award — Yoga & Fitness: Simone Sharice For a personalized wellness companion that answers, “What should I do today?” Judges will consider how effectively the app turns movement, Pilates, recovery, and other wellness needs into a clear, achievable daily plan without creating more information overload. Influencer Award — Career Coaching: Leadership Heather For an app that helps new managers practise difficult workplace conversations before the stakes are real. Judges are looking for realistic scenarios, useful feedback, confidence-building experiences, and active practice with situations such as feedback, boundaries, and saying no. Influencer Award — Gaming: Mr Lewis Blogs Gaming For a gaming bucket-list app that makes it easy to save games at the moment of discovery. Judges will consider how effectively users can organize, complete, rate, and share games, along with whether managing a backlog feels enjoyable rather than like another chore. Ship Kotlin Everywhere — JetBrains Recognizes a creative, polished app built for both iOS and Android using Kotlin Multiplatform, Compose Multiplatform, or both. Judges will consider cross-platform quality, consistency, and effective use of Kotlin. Optional consideration may be given to useful build content and contributions to the Kotlin Multiplatform community. Most Viral App — Noise Awarded to the app that captures the most attention in its market through high-quality, scalable content that converts into downloads. Judges will consider virality, whether the creative formats can be repeated at scale, and how clearly the content communicates the app’s value and addresses users’ needs. Best App for Galaxy — Samsung Recognizes a high-quality app published on the Galaxy Store and thoughtfully optimized for Samsung Galaxy users. Judges will consider the overall app experience and Galaxy-specific optimization, including foldable-device support, Samsung features, and device performance. Galaxy Store exclusivity may receive bonus consideration but is not required. Replit’s Idea to Income Recognizes a project that uses Replit to turn a new idea into a live, monetizing mobile app. Judges will primarily consider consistent week-over-week growth in revenue and transactions, supported by paying-user traction, product craft, visual design, and meaningful community engagement. Keep Them Coming Back Award — OneSignal Recognizes an app that uses OneSignal thoughtfully to bring users back. Judges will consider the quality and stability of the implementation, the value it adds to the user experience, and how creatively the app uses campaigns, push notifications, Journeys, or advanced messaging capabilities. The Growth Loop Award — Layers Recognizes a team that treats growth as a process of testing, measuring, learning, and improving. Judges will consider the clarity of the audience and growth hypothesis, how Layers was used to run and observe a focused experiment, whether the SDK was installed correctly, and what the team learned or would try next. Funnel Vision Award — Stripe Recognizes a project that launches a web funnel using RevenueCat Funnels and Stripe. Judges will consider the qualifying web payment volume processed during the measurement period and whether the funnel is thoughtfully designed, functional, and effectively implemented. Prize structure You can find the official details of prizes at the bottom of this page, but here's how it all breaks down: Grand Prize Winner $100,000 Trip to New York City for the Shippies award ceremony and RevenueCat's App Growth Annual conference Custom Shippy trophy (presented live on stage!) App featured on a massive Times Square billboard Media spotlight on 9to5Mac and 9to5Google #BuildInPublic Category 1st Place: $30,000 + custom Shippy trophy + Times Square billboard feature + media spotlight + Trip to New York City for the Shippies award ceremony and RevenueCat's App Growth Annual conference 2nd Place: $20,000 3rd Place: $10,000 OneSignal's Keep Them Coming Back Award winner 1st Place: $25,000 + custom Shippy trophy + Times Square billboard feature + media spotlight 2nd Place: $15,000 3rd Place: $5,000 All Other Categories 1st Place: $20,000 + custom Shippy trophy + Times Square billboard feature + media spotlight 2nd Place: $10,000 3rd Place: $5,000 Supported by the industry This year, our sponsors have shown up big. Huge thanks to Replit, OneSignal, JetBrains, Layers, Noise, Stripe, and Samsung for coming in as category sponsors for Shipaton 2026. And more sponsors are joining the fun all the time, which means bigger cash prizes and more additions to the Ship Kit. Ship Kit is back: Freebies for every Shipaton participant Ship Kit is your bundle of tools, credits, deals, and resources from our sponsors to help you build faster, launch better, and save a lot of money along the way. Some deals are while supplies last, so the sooner you register at the top of this page, the sooner you get access as Ship Kit starts to roll out. The #ShipatonSale If you have an app, tool, service, course, or template that could help Shipaton builders, run a sale for participants and share it with the #ShipatonSale hashtag. Submit it on the Shipaton website and we'll list community sales for everyone to find. Even if you're not competing, there are ways to support the builders who are. Shipaton IRL: Events near you We're excited to take Shipaton directly to developers around the world with Shipaton IRL. Last year, builders gathered in Tokyo, Seoul, London, St. Louis, Barcelona, Delhi, Vancouver, Warsaw, Skopje, and dozens of cities in between. This year, we want even more: kickoff parties, co-working days, weekend build sprints, launch-day meetups, and campus hackathons. Check out the events page regularly, as new events are being added all the time! Want to host a Shipaton event yourself? Apply now - we'd love to support you. Approved hosts get a Meetup-in-a-box with Shipaton swag, food vouchers, and organizer resources, and we'll promote your event to the massive Shipaton audience. Perfect for developer communities, hacker clubs, and student organizers planning campus events. Join the conversation on Discord! Shipaton isn't just about shipping code - it's about community. Whether you're brainstorming your first idea or prepping for launch day, the official Shipaton Discord is the place to connect, collaborate, and share the journey. Inside, you'll find fellow builders from around the world debugging code, running paywall experiments, discussing launch strategies, and more. Looking to form a team? Need quick feedback? Want to hang out with other shippers? You'll find it here. We've also created a dedicated #post-engagement-boost channel where you can share your YouTube videos, posts, and other #BuildInPublic content so other participants can like, comment, or share to help you reach a bigger audience. It's all about creating a positive, encouraging space where we lift each other - and help each other ship. Shipaton Livestreams Throughout the event, we'll host twice-a-week livestreams with expert guests, practical sessions, and live Q&A — so you're never building alone for two months. Come say hi 👋 and make the most of Shipaton! Ready, set, ship! Submissions open on August 1st and close on September 30th. Be sure to carefully review all submission requirements to ensure your app qualifies. We're beyond excited to see what the global builder community creates this year. Register today, and we'll keep you updated via the email address you use there. Let's get shipping! Requirements WHAT TO BUILD Entrants must create a working software application that uses the RevenueCat SDK to power at least one in-app or web purchase (each a "Project"). Apps must be built for iOS, iPadOS, macOS, or Android. The first public version of your app must be released between August 1 and September 30, 2026 . Students competing for the Next Gen Award follow a different, lower-friction path: submit a video and source code instead of a published store listing. No paid Apple or Google developer account required. Students under the age of majority where they reside may enter the Next Gen Award (minimum age 13) with parent or guardian consent. See Section 3 of the official rules. What to submit on Devpost Every submission must include: A text description of your app's features and functionality. A demo video of your project. The video: Should show the app running on the device it was built for. Must be no longer than 2 minutes of essential footage — judges are not required to watch beyond two minutes. Must be uploaded to and publicly visible on YouTube or Vimeo, with the link provided on this form. Must not include third-party trademarks or copyrighted music/material unless you have permission to use it. A URL to your fully published app on the App Store or Google Play or Samsung Galaxy Store. A 1024×1024 app icon . At least one screenshot of the app at 1179px × 2556px with no device frame . Either a free trial in your app, or a promo code so judges can unlock the in-app purchase and test all premium features. Join hackathon Who can participate Ages 13 to 99 only Specific countries/territories excluded View full rules October 01 at 2:45am EDT to deadline View schedule Deadline: Sep 30, 2026 @ 11:45pm PDT Apple Google Outlook Online Public $ 740,000 in cash 23849 participants RevenueCat Design Gaming Mobile Welcome to the RevenueCat Shipaton — the mobile hackathon that's all about shipping… a ton. At RevenueCat, we're all about supporting developers to build and monetize amazing apps. After the overwhelming success of last year's Shipaton, we're thrilled to announce the return of our global hackathon — and this year, we're going bigger than ever. This August and September, we're inviting builders from all corners of the globe to ship new apps and compete for over $700,000 in cash prizes and truly unique rewards — over $1 million worth of prizes in total. The challenge Ship a brand-new app to the App Store, Google Play Store, or — new this year — the Samsung Galaxy Store, between August 1st and September 30th, 2026. Integrate the RevenueCat SDK to power at least one in-app purchase or serve ads through RevenueCat Ads. Our goal is to give you that final push to ship that project you've had in the back of your mind but never took the time to get started. Note: Updates to previously released apps won't qualify - it's all about bringing something new to life! You can brainstorm, build, and post before August 1st, but your app must be released for the first time during the Shipaton window. Bigger and better Last year's Shipaton blew us away. Hundreds of new apps launched, thousands of #BuildInPublic posts went out, communities from Tokyo to Seoul to London hosted Shipaton IRL events, and winning teams ended up on stage in New York, accepting their Shippy trophies with their apps lighting up a Times Square billboard. Inspired by your amazing contributions, we've upped the ante for 2026: Over $700,000 in cash prizes — and growing as more sponsors join. Winning apps featured on giant billboards in Times Square. Flights to New York City for the Shippies red carpet award ceremony and RevenueCat's App Growth Annual conference. Press coverage for winners on 9to5Mac and 9to5Google. NEW: Investor exposure through the Shipaton Growth Fund. Categories Grand Prize: Goes to the app that gains the most user traction and growth momentum during the event. We want to hear about what you've done post-release to push your app growth to the next level. [NEW] Next Gen Award: A student-only category for the best app submitted by active students — high school, university, bootcamp, campus dev club, anyone learning the craft. Judged on a video submission and open-source code, so no paid Apple or Google developer account is required. Open to students 13 and up. If you're under the age of majority where you live, a parent or guardian just needs to consent and agree to the rules on your behalf. Learn more on the Next Gen page . [NEW] Catvertising Award: Celebrates the most creative and effective use of RevenueCat Ads as a monetization method. We're looking for clever placements, smart integration with the rest of the revenue stack, and an experience users don't hate. [NEW] Best Game Award: For the best mobile game shipped during the event. We're looking for great gameplay, art direction, and a monetization fit that suits the genre. #BuildInPublic Award: For developers who share the most interesting development journey on social media. We're looking for compelling lessons learned or clever ideas that came from engaging with the community. HAMM Award (Help Apps Make Money): RevenueCat exists to "Help Apps Make More Money". This award goes to the project that designs the most robust and creative monetization strategy. RevenueCat Design Award: For the app that best represents the craft of app development — regardless of business potential. We're looking for innovative ideas and/or beautiful app design and animations. RevenueCat Peace Prize: Awarded to the project that provides the greatest social good. We're looking for apps with big benefits to communities or society at large. Conflict of Interest Award: A special category for RevenueCat employees and sponsors who couldn't resist joining the fun. No cash prizes, but a shot at glory. Influencer Award — Productivity: Christopher Lawley For a polished productivity app that gives Apple power users one fast, focused place to save and retrieve reusable text snippets, documents, files, and images. Judges will consider product focus, speed, organization, intelligent features, and the quality of the overall design. Influencer Award — Nutrition & Healthy Eating: Abbey’s Kitchen For a flexible nutrition app inspired by Abbey’s Hunger Crushing Combo framework. Judges are looking for a compassionate, practical experience that helps users create more satisfying meals in real-life situations without calorie counting, macro tracking, or restrictive meal plans. Influencer Award — Yoga & Fitness: Simone Sharice For a personalized wellness companion that answers, “What should I do today?” Judges will consider how effectively the app turns movement, Pilates, recovery, and other wellness needs into a clear, achievable daily plan without creating more information overload. Influencer Award — Career Coaching: Leadership Heather For an app that helps new managers practise difficult workplace conversations before the stakes are real. Judges are looking for realistic scenarios, useful feedback, confidence-building experiences, and active practice with situations such as feedback, boundaries, and saying no. Influencer Award — Gaming: Mr Lewis Blogs Gaming For a gaming bucket-list app that makes it easy to save games at the moment of discovery. Judges will consider how effectively users can organize, complete, rate, and share games, along with whether managing a backlog feels enjoyable rather than like another chore. Ship Kotlin Everywhere — JetBrains Recognizes a creative, polished app built for both iOS and Android using Kotlin Multiplatform, Compose Multiplatform, or both. Judges will consider cross-platform quality, consistency, and effective use of Kotlin. Optional consideration may be given to useful build content and contributions to the Kotlin Multiplatform community. Most Viral App — Noise Awarded to the app that captures the most attention in its market through high-quality, scalable content that converts into downloads. Judges will consider virality, whether the creative formats can be repeated at scale, and how clearly the content communicates the app’s value and addresses users’ needs. Best App for Galaxy — Samsung Recognizes a high-quality app published on the Galaxy Store and thoughtfully optimized for Samsung Galaxy users. Judges will consider the overall app experience and Galaxy-specific optimization, including foldable-device support, Samsung features, and device performance. Galaxy Store exclusivity may receive bonus consideration but is not required. Replit’s Idea to Income Recognizes a project that uses Replit to turn a new idea into a live, monetizing mobile app. Judges will primarily consider consistent week-over-week growth in revenue and transactions, supported by paying-user traction, product craft, visual design, and meaningful community engagement. Keep Them Coming Back Award — OneSignal Recognizes an app that uses OneSignal thoughtfully to bring users back. Judges will consider the quality and stability of the implementation, the value it adds to the user experience, and how creatively the app uses campaigns, push notifications, Journeys, or advanced messaging capabilities. The Growth Loop Award — Layers Recognizes a team that treats growth as a process of testing, measuring, learning, and improving. Judges will consider the clarity of the audience and growth hypothesis, how Layers was used to run and observe a focused experiment, whether the SDK was installed correctly, and what the team learned or would try next. Funnel Vision Award — Stripe Recognizes a project that launches a web funnel using RevenueCat Funnels and Stripe. Judges will consider the qualifying web payment volume processed during the measurement period and whether the funnel is thoughtfully designed, functional, and effectively implemented. Prize structure You can find the official details of prizes at the bottom of this page, but here's how it all breaks down: Grand Prize Winner $100,000 Trip to New York City for the Shippies award ceremony and RevenueCat's App Growth Annual conference Custom Shippy trophy (presented live on stage!) App featured on a massive Times Square billboard Media spotlight on 9to5Mac and 9to5Google #BuildInPublic Category 1st Place: $30,000 + custom Shippy trophy + Times Square billboard feature + media spotlight + Trip to New York City for the Shippies award ceremony and RevenueCat's App Growth Annual conference 2nd Place: $20,000 3rd Place: $10,000 OneSignal's Keep Them Coming Back Award winner 1st Place: $25,000 + custom Shippy trophy + Times Square billboard feature + media spotlight 2nd Place: $15,000 3rd Place: $5,000 All Other Categories 1st Place: $20,000 + custom Shippy trophy + Times Square billboard feature + media spotlight 2nd Place: $10,000 3rd Place: $5,000 Supported by the industry This year, our sponsors have shown up big. Huge thanks to Replit, OneSignal, JetBrains, Layers, Noise, Stripe, and Samsung for coming in as category sponsors for Shipaton 2026. And more sponsors are joining the fun all the time, which means bigger cash prizes and more additions to the Ship Kit. Ship Kit is back: Freebies for every Shipaton participant Ship Kit is your bundle of tools, credits, deals, and resources from our sponsors to help you build faster, launch better, and save a lot of money along the way. Some deals are while supplies last, so the sooner you register at the top of this page, the sooner you get access as Ship Kit starts to roll out. The #ShipatonSale If you have an app, tool, service, course, or template that could help Shipaton builders, run a sale for participants and share it with the #ShipatonSale hashtag. Submit it on the Shipaton website and we'll list community sales for everyone to find. Even if you're not competing, there are ways to support the builders who are. Shipaton IRL: Events near you We're excited to take Shipaton directly to developers around the world with Shipaton IRL. Last year, builders gathered in Tokyo, Seoul, London, St. Louis, Barcelona, Delhi, Vancouver, Warsaw, Skopje, and dozens of cities in between. This year, we want even more: kickoff parties, co-working days, weekend build sprints, launch-day meetups, and campus hackathons. Check out the events page regularly, as new events are being added all the time! Want to host a Shipaton event yourself? Apply now - we'd love to support you. Approved hosts get a Meetup-in-a-box with Shipaton swag, food vouchers, and organizer resources, and we'll promote your event to the massive Shipaton audience. Perfect for developer communities, hacker clubs, and student organizers planning campus events. Join the conversation on Discord! Shipaton isn't just about shipping code - it's about community. Whether you're brainstorming your first idea or prepping for launch day, the official Shipaton Discord is the place to connect, collaborate, and share the journey. Inside, you'll find fellow builders from around the world debugging code, running paywall experiments, discussing launch strategies, and more. Looking to form a team? Need quick feedback? Want to hang out with other shippers? You'll find it here. We've also created a dedicated #post-engagement-boost channel where you can share your YouTube videos, posts, and other #BuildInPublic content so other participants can like, comment, or share to help you reach a bigger audience. It's all about creating a positive, encouraging space where we lift each other - and help each other ship. Shipaton Livestreams Throughout the event, we'll host twice-a-week livestreams with expert guests, practical sessions, and live Q&A — so you're never building alone for two months. Come say hi 👋 and make the most of Shipaton! Ready, set, ship! Submissions open on August 1st and close on September 30th. Be sure to carefully review all submission requirements to ensure your app qualifies. We're beyond excited to see what the global builder community creates this year. Register today, and we'll keep you updated via the email address you use there. Let's get shipping! Requirements WHAT TO BUILD Entrants must create a working software application that uses the RevenueCat SDK to power at least one in-app or web purchase (each a "Project"). Apps must be built for iOS, iPadOS, macOS, or Android. The first public version of your app must be released between August 1 and September 30, 2026 . Students competing for the Next Gen Award follow a different, lower-friction path: submit a video and source code instead of a published store listing. No paid Apple or Google developer account required. Students under the age of majority where they reside may enter the Next Gen Award (minimum age 13) with parent or guardian consent. See Section 3 of the official rules. What to submit on Devpost Every submission must include: A text description of your app's features and functionality. A demo video of your project. The video: Should show the app running on the device it was built for. Must be no longer than 2 minutes of essential footage — judges are not required to watch beyond two minutes. Must be uploaded to and publicly visible on YouTube or Vimeo, with the link provided on this form. Must not include third-party trademarks or copyrighted music/material unless you have permission to use it. A URL to your fully published app on the App Store or Google Play or Samsung Galaxy Store. A 1024×1024 app icon . At least one screenshot of the app at 1179px × 2556px with no device frame . Either a free trial in your app, or a promo code so judges can unlock the in-app purchase and test all premium features. Join hackathon Who can participate Ages 13 to 99 only Specific countries/territories excluded View full rules October 01 at 2:45am EDT to deadline View schedule Deadline: Sep 30, 2026 @ 11:45pm PDT Apple Google Outlook Online Public $ 740,000 in cash 23849 participants RevenueCat Design Gaming Mobile Welcome to the RevenueCat Shipaton — the mobile hackathon that's all about shipping… a ton. At RevenueCat, we're all about supporting developers to build and monetize amazing apps. After the overwhelming success of last year's Shipaton, we're thrilled to announce the return of our global hackathon — and this year, we're going bigger than ever. This August and September, we're inviting builders from all corners of the globe to ship new apps and compete for over $700,000 in cash prizes and truly unique rewards — over $1 million worth of prizes in total. The challenge Ship a brand-new app to the App Store, Google Play Store, or — new this year — the Samsung Galaxy Store, between August 1st and September 30th, 2026. Integrate the RevenueCat SDK to power at least one in-app purchase or serve ads through RevenueCat Ads. Our goal is to give you that final push to ship that project you've had in the back of your mind but never took the time to get started. Note: Updates to previously released apps won't qualify - it's all about bringing something new to life! You can brainstorm, build, and post before August 1st, but your app must be released for the first time during the Shipaton window. Bigger and better Last year's Shipaton blew us away. Hundreds of new apps launched, thousands of #BuildInPublic posts went out, communities from Tokyo to Seoul to London hosted Shipaton IRL events, and winning teams ended up on stage in New York, accepting their Shippy trophies with their apps lighting up a Times Square billboard. Inspired by your amazing contributions, we've upped the ante for 2026: Over $700,000 in cash prizes — and growing as more sponsors join. Winning apps featured on giant billboards in Times Square. Flights to New York City for the Shippies red carpet award ceremony and RevenueCat's App Growth Annual conference. Press coverage for winners on 9to5Mac and 9to5Google. NEW: Investor exposure through the Shipaton Growth Fund. Categories Grand Prize: Goes to the app that gains the most user traction and growth momentum during the event. We want to hear about what you've done post-release to push your app growth to the next level. [NEW] Next Gen Award: A student-only category for the best app submitted by active students — high school, university, bootcamp, campus dev club, anyone learning the craft. Judged on a video submission and open-source code, so no paid Apple or Google developer account is required. Open to students 13 and up. If you're under the age of majority where you live, a parent or guardian just needs to consent and agree to the rules on your behalf. Learn more on the Next Gen page . [NEW] Catvertising Award: Celebrates the most creative and effective use of RevenueCat Ads as a monetization method. We're looking for clever placements, smart integration with the rest of the revenue stack, and an experience users don't hate. [NEW] Best Game Award: For the best mobile game shipped during the event. We're looking for great gameplay, art direction, and a monetization fit that suits the genre. #BuildInPublic Award: For developers who share the most interesting development journey on social media. We're looking for compelling lessons learned or clever ideas that came from engaging with the community. HAMM Award (Help Apps Make Money): RevenueCat exists to "Help Apps Make More Money". This award goes to the project that designs the most robust and creative monetization strategy. RevenueCat Design Award: For the app that best represents the craft of app development — regardless of business potential. We're looking for innovative ideas and/or beautiful app design and animations. RevenueCat Peace Prize: Awarded to the project that provides the greatest social good. We're looking for apps with big benefits to communities or society at large. Conflict of Interest Award: A special category for RevenueCat employees and sponsors who couldn't resist joining the fun. No cash prizes, but a shot at glory. Influencer Award — Productivity: Christopher Lawley For a polished productivity app that gives Apple power users one fast, focused place to save and retrieve reusable text snippets, documents, files, and images. Judges will consider product focus, speed, organization, intelligent features, and the quality of the overall design. Influencer Award — Nutrition & Healthy Eating: Abbey’s Kitchen For a flexible nutrition app inspired by Abbey’s Hunger Crushing Combo framework. Judges are looking for a compassionate, practical experience that helps users create more satisfying meals in real-life situations without calorie counting, macro tracking, or restrictive meal plans. Influencer Award — Yoga & Fitness: Simone Sharice For a personalized wellness companion that answers, “What should I do today?” Judges will consider how effectively the app turns movement, Pilates, recovery, and other wellness needs into a clear, achievable daily plan without creating more information overload. Influencer Award — Career Coaching: Leadership Heather For an app that helps new managers practise difficult workplace conversations before the stakes are real. Judges are looking for realistic scenarios, useful feedback, confidence-building experiences, and active practice with situations such as feedback, boundaries, and saying no. Influencer Award — Gaming: Mr Lewis Blogs Gaming For a gaming bucket-list app that makes it easy to save games at the moment of discovery. Judges will consider how effectively users can organize, complete, rate, and share games, along with whether managing a backlog feels enjoyable rather than like another chore. Ship Kotlin Everywhere — JetBrains Recognizes a creative, polished app built for both iOS and Android using Kotlin Multiplatform, Compose Multiplatform, or both. Judges will consider cross-platform quality, consistency, and effective use of Kotlin. Optional consideration may be given to useful build content and contributions to the Kotlin Multiplatform community. Most Viral App — Noise Awarded to the app that captures the most attention in its market through high-quality, scalable content that converts into downloads. Judges will consider virality, whether the creative formats can be repeated at scale, and how clearly the content communicates the app’s value and addresses users’ needs. Best App for Galaxy — Samsung Recognizes a high-quality app published on the Galaxy Store and thoughtfully optimized for Samsung Galaxy users. Judges will consider the overall app experience and Galaxy-specific optimization, including foldable-device support, Samsung features, and device performance. Galaxy Store exclusivity may receive bonus consideration but is not required. Replit’s Idea to Income Recognizes a project that uses Replit to turn a new idea into a live, monetizing mobile app. Judges will primarily consider consistent week-over-week growth in revenue and transactions, supported by paying-user traction, product craft, visual design, and meaningful community engagement. Keep Them Coming Back Award — OneSignal Recognizes an app that uses OneSignal thoughtfully to bring users back. Judges will consider the quality and stability of the implementation, the value it adds to the user experience, and how creatively the app uses campaigns, push notifications, Journeys, or advanced messaging capabilities. The Growth Loop Award — Layers Recognizes a team that treats growth as a process of testing, measuring, learning, and improving. Judges will consider the clarity of the audience and growth hypothesis, how Layers was used to run and observe a focused experiment, whether the SDK was installed correctly, and what the team learned or would try next. Funnel Vision Award — Stripe Recognizes a project that launches a web funnel using RevenueCat Funnels and Stripe. Judges will consider the qualifying web payment volume processed during the measurement period and whether the funnel is thoughtfully designed, functional, and effectively implemented. Prize structure You can find the official details of prizes at the bottom of this page, but here's how it all breaks down: Grand Prize Winner $100,000 Trip to New York City for the Shippies award ceremony and RevenueCat's App Growth Annual conference Custom Shippy trophy (presented live on stage!) App featured on a massive Times Square billboard Media spotlight on 9to5Mac and 9to5Google #BuildInPublic Category 1st Place: $30,000 + custom Shippy trophy + Times Square billboard feature + media spotlight + Trip to New York City for the Shippies award ceremony and RevenueCat's App Growth Annual conference 2nd Place: $20,000 3rd Place: $10,000 OneSignal's Keep Them Coming Back Award winner 1st Place: $25,000 + custom Shippy trophy + Times Square billboard feature + media spotlight 2nd Place: $15,000 3rd Place: $5,000 All Other Categories 1st Place: $20,000 + custom Shippy trophy + Times Square billboard feature + media spotlight 2nd Place: $10,000 3rd Place: $5,000 Supported by the industry This year, our sponsors have shown up big. Huge thanks to Replit, OneSignal, JetBrains, Layers, Noise, Stripe, and Samsung for coming in as category sponsors for Shipaton 2026. And more sponsors are joining the fun all the time, which means bigger cash prizes and more additions to the Ship Kit. Ship Kit is back: Freebies for every Shipaton participant Ship Kit is your bundle of tools, credits, deals, and resources from our sponsors to help you build faster, launch better, and save a lot of money along the way. Some deals are while supplies last, so the sooner you register at the top of this page, the sooner you get access as Ship Kit starts to roll out. The #ShipatonSale If you have an app, tool, service, course, or template that could help Shipaton builders, run a sale for participants and share it with the #ShipatonSale hashtag. Submit it on the Shipaton website and we'll list community sales for everyone to find. Even if you're not competing, there are ways to support the builders who are. Shipaton IRL: Events near you We're excited to take Shipaton directly to developers around the world with Shipaton IRL. Last year, builders gathered in Tokyo, Seoul, London, St. Louis, Barcelona, Delhi, Vancouver, Warsaw, Skopje, and dozens of cities in between. This year, we want even more: kickoff parties, co-working days, weekend build sprints, launch-day meetups, and campus hackathons. Check out the events page regularly, as new events are being added all the time! Want to host a Shipaton event yourself? Apply now - we'd love to support you. Approved hosts get a Meetup-in-a-box with Shipaton swag, food vouchers, and organizer resources, and we'll promote your event to the massive Shipaton audience. Perfect for developer communities, hacker clubs, and student organizers planning campus events. Join the conversation on Discord! Shipaton isn't just about shipping code - it's about community. Whether you're brainstorming your first idea or prepping for launch day, the official Shipaton Discord is the place to connect, collaborate, and share the journey. Inside, you'll find fellow builders from around the world debugging code, running paywall experiments, discussing launch strategies, and more. Looking to form a team? Need quick feedback? Want to hang out with other shippers? You'll find it here. We've also created a dedicated #post-engagement-boost channel where you can share your YouTube videos, posts, and other #BuildInPublic content so other participants can like, comment, or share to help you reach a bigger audience. It's all about creating a positive, encouraging space where we lift each other - and help each other ship. Shipaton Livestreams Throughout the event, we'll host twice-a-week livestreams with expert guests, practical sessions, and live Q&A — so you're never building alone for two months. Come say hi 👋 and make the most of Shipaton! Ready, set, ship! Submissions open on August 1st and close on September 30th. Be sure to carefully review all submission requirements to ensure your app qualifies. We're beyond excited to see what the global builder community creates this year. Register today, and we'll keep you updated via the email address you use there. Let's get shipping! Requirements WHAT TO BUILD Entrants must create a working software application that uses the RevenueCat SDK to power at least one in-app or web purchase (each a "Project"). Apps must be built for iOS, iPadOS, macOS, or Android. The first public version of your app must be released between August 1 and September 30, 2026 . Students competing for the Next Gen Award follow a different, lower-friction path: submit a video and source code instead of a published store listing. No paid Apple or Google developer account required. Students under the age of majority where they reside may enter the Next Gen Award (minimum age 13) with parent or guardian consent. See Section 3 of the official rules. What to submit on Devpost Every submission must include: A text description of your app's features and functionality. A demo video of your project. The video: Should show the app running on the device it was built for. Must be no longer than 2 minutes of essential footage — judges are not required to watch beyond two minutes. Must be uploaded to and publicly visible on YouTube or Vimeo, with the link provided on this form. Must not include third-party trademarks or copyrighted music/material unless you have permission to use it. A URL to your fully published app on the App Store or Google Play or Samsung Galaxy Store. A 1024×1024 app icon . At least one screenshot of the app at 1179px × 2556px with no device frame . Either a free trial in your app, or a promo code so judges can unlock the in-app purchase and test all premium features. Join hackathon Who can participate Ages 13 to 99 only Specific countries/territories excluded View full rules October 01 at 2:45am EDT to deadline View schedule Deadline: Sep 30, 2026 @ 11:45pm PDT Apple Google Outlook Online Public $ 740,000 in cash 23849 participants RevenueCat Design Gaming Mobile Welcome to the RevenueCat Shipaton — the mobile hackathon that's all about shipping… a ton. At RevenueCat, we're all about supporting developers to build and monetize amazing apps. After the overwhelming success of last year's Shipaton, we're thrilled to announce the return of our global hackathon — and this year, we're going bigger than ever. This August and September, we're inviting builders from all corners of the globe to ship new apps and compete for over $700,000 in cash prizes and truly unique rewards — over $1 million worth of prizes in total. The challenge Ship a brand-new app to the App Store, Google Play Store, or — new this year — the Samsung Galaxy Store, between August 1st and September 30th, 2026. Integrate the RevenueCat SDK to power at least one in-app purchase or serve ads through RevenueCat Ads. Our goal is to give you that final push to ship that project you've had in the back of your mind but never took the time to get started. Note: Updates to previously released apps won't qualify - it's all about bringing something new to life! You can brainstorm, build, and post before August 1st, but your app must be released for the first time during the Shipaton window. Bigger and better Last year's Shipaton blew us away. Hundreds of new apps launched, thousands of #BuildInPublic posts went out, communities from Tokyo to Seoul to London hosted Shipaton IRL events, and winning teams ended up on stage in New York, accepting their Shippy trophies with their apps lighting up a Times Square billboard. Inspired by your amazing contributions, we've upped the ante for 2026: Over $700,000 in cash prizes — and growing as more sponsors join. Winning apps featured on giant billboards in Times Square. Flights to New York City for the Shippies red carpet award ceremony and RevenueCat's App Growth Annual conference. Press coverage for winners on 9to5Mac and 9to5Google. NEW: Investor exposure through the Shipaton Growth Fund. Categories Grand Prize: Goes to the app that gains the most user traction and growth momentum during the event. We want to hear about what you've done post-release to push your app growth to the next level. [NEW] Next Gen Award: A student-only category for the best app submitted by active students — high school, university, bootcamp, campus dev club, anyone learning the craft. Judged on a video submission and open-source code, so no paid Apple or Google developer account is required. Open to students 13 and up. If you're under the age of majority where you live, a parent or guardian just needs to consent and agree to the rules on your behalf. Learn more on the Next Gen page . [NEW] Catvertising Award: Celebrates the most creative and effective use of RevenueCat Ads as a monetization method. We're looking for clever placements, smart integration with the rest of the revenue stack, and an experience users don't hate. [NEW] Best Game Award: For the best mobile game shipped during the event. We're looking for great gameplay, art direction, and a monetization fit that suits the genre. #BuildInPublic Award: For developers who share the most interesting development journey on social media. We're looking for compelling lessons learned or clever ideas that came from engaging with the community. HAMM Award (Help Apps Make Money): RevenueCat exists to "Help Apps Make More Money". This award goes to the project that designs the most robust and creative monetization strategy. RevenueCat Design Award: For the app that best represents the craft of app development — regardless of business potential. We're looking for innovative ideas and/or beautiful app design and animations. RevenueCat Peace Prize: Awarded to the project that provides the greatest social good. We're looking for apps with big benefits to communities or society at large. Conflict of Interest Award: A special category for RevenueCat employees and sponsors who couldn't resist joining the fun. No cash prizes, but a shot at glory. Influencer Award — Productivity: Christopher Lawley For a polished productivity app that gives Apple power users one fast, focused place to save and retrieve reusable text snippets, documents, files, and images. Judges will consider product focus, speed, organization, intelligent features, and the quality of the overall design. Influencer Award — Nutrition & Healthy Eating: Abbey’s Kitchen For a flexible nutrition app inspired by Abbey’s Hunger Crushing Combo framework. Judges are looking for a compassionate, practical experience that helps users create more satisfying meals in real-life situations without calorie counting, macro tracking, or restrictive meal plans. Influencer Award — Yoga & Fitness: Simone Sharice For a personalized wellness companion that answers, “What should I do today?” Judges will consider how effectively the app turns movement, Pilates, recovery, and other wellness needs into a clear, achievable daily plan without creating more information overload. Influencer Award — Career Coaching: Leadership Heather For an app that helps new managers practise difficult workplace conversations before the stakes are real. Judges are looking for realistic scenarios, useful feedback, confidence-building experiences, and active practice with situations such as feedback, boundaries, and saying no. Influencer Award — Gaming: Mr Lewis Blogs Gaming For a gaming bucket-list app that makes it easy to save games at the moment of discovery. Judges will consider how effectively users can organize, complete, rate, and share games, along with whether managing a backlog feels enjoyable rather than like another chore. Ship Kotlin Everywhere — JetBrains Recognizes a creative, polished app built for both iOS and Android using Kotlin Multiplatform, Compose Multiplatform, or both. Judges will consider cross-platform quality, consistency, and effective use of Kotlin. Optional consideration may be given to useful build content and contributions to the Kotlin Multiplatform community. Most Viral App — Noise Awarded to the app that captures the most attention in its market through high-quality, scalable content that converts into downloads. Judges will consider virality, whether the creative formats can be repeated at scale, and how clearly the content communicates the app’s value and addresses users’ needs. Best App for Galaxy — Samsung Recognizes a high-quality app published on the Galaxy Store and thoughtfully optimized for Samsung Galaxy users. Judges will consider the overall app experience and Galaxy-specific optimization, including foldable-device support, Samsung features, and device performance. Galaxy Store exclusivity may receive bonus consideration but is not required. Replit’s Idea to Income Recognizes a project that uses Replit to turn a new idea into a live, monetizing mobile app. Judges will primarily consider consistent week-over-week growth in revenue and transactions, supported by paying-user traction, product craft, visual design, and meaningful community engagement. Keep Them Coming Back Award — OneSignal Recognizes an app that uses OneSignal thoughtfully to bring users back. Judges will consider the quality and stability of the implementation, the value it adds to the user experience, and how creatively the app uses campaigns, push notifications, Journeys, or advanced messaging capabilities. The Growth Loop Award — Layers Recognizes a team that treats growth as a process of testing, measuring, learning, and improving. Judges will consider the clarity of the audience and growth hypothesis, how Layers was used to run and observe a focused experiment, whether the SDK was installed correctly, and what the team learned or would try next. Funnel Vision Award — Stripe Recognizes a project that launches a web funnel using RevenueCat Funnels and Stripe. Judges will consider the qualifying web payment volume processed during the measurement period and whether the funnel is thoughtfully designed, functional, and effectively implemented. Prize structure You can find the official details of prizes at the bottom of this page, but here's how it all breaks down: Grand Prize Winner $100,000 Trip to New York City for the Shippies award ceremony and RevenueCat's App Growth Annual conference Custom Shippy trophy (presented live on stage!) App featured on a massive Times Square billboard Media spotlight on 9to5Mac and 9to5Google #BuildInPublic Category 1st Place: $30,000 + custom Shippy trophy + Times Square billboard feature + media spotlight + Trip to New York City for the Shippies award ceremony and RevenueCat's App Growth Annual conference 2nd Place: $20,000 3rd Place: $10,000 OneSignal's Keep Them Coming Back Award winner 1st Place: $25,000 + custom Shippy trophy + Times Square billboard feature + media spotlight 2nd Place: $15,000 3rd Place: $5,000 All Other Categories 1st Place: $20,000 + custom Shippy trophy + Times Square billboard feature + media spotlight 2nd Place: $10,000 3rd Place: $5,000 Supported by the industry This year, our sponsors have shown up big. Huge thanks to Replit, OneSignal, JetBrains, Layers, Noise, Stripe, and Samsung for coming in as category sponsors for Shipaton 2026. And more sponsors are joining the fun all the time, which means bigger cash prizes and more additions to the Ship Kit. Ship Kit is back: Freebies for every Shipaton participant Ship Kit is your bundle of tools, credits, deals, and resources from our sponsors to help you build faster, launch better, and save a lot of money along the way. Some deals are while supplies last, so the sooner you register at the top of this page, the sooner you get access as Ship Kit starts to roll out. The #ShipatonSale If you have an app, tool, service, course, or template that could help Shipaton builders, run a sale for participants and share it with the #ShipatonSale hashtag. Submit it on the Shipaton website and we'll list community sales for everyone to find. Even if you're not competing, there are ways to support the builders who are. Shipaton IRL: Events near you We're excited to take Shipaton directly to developers around the world with Shipaton IRL. Last year, builders gathered in Tokyo, Seoul, London, St. Louis, Barcelona, Delhi, Vancouver, Warsaw, Skopje, and dozens of cities in between. This year, we want even more: kickoff parties, co-working days, weekend build sprints, launch-day meetups, and campus hackathons. Check out the events page regularly, as new events are being added all the time! Want to host a Shipaton event yourself? Apply now - we'd love to support you. Approved hosts get a Meetup-in-a-box with Shipaton swag, food vouchers, and organizer resources, and we'll promote your event to the massive Shipaton audience. Perfect for developer communities, hacker clubs, and student organizers planning campus events. Join the conversation on Discord! Shipaton isn't just about shipping code - it's about community. Whether you're brainstorming your first idea or prepping for launch day, the official Shipaton Discord is the place to connect, collaborate, and share the journey. Inside, you'll find fellow builders from around the world debugging code, running paywall experiments, discussing launch strategies, and more. Looking to form a team? Need quick feedback? Want to hang out with other shippers? You'll find it here. We've also created a dedicated #post-engagement-boost channel where you can share your YouTube videos, posts, and other #BuildInPublic content so other participants can like, comment, or share to help you reach a bigger audience. It's all about creating a positive, encouraging space where we lift each other - and help each other ship. Shipaton Livestreams Throughout the event, we'll host twice-a-week livestreams with expert guests, practical sessions, and live Q&A — so you're never building alone for two months. Come say hi 👋 and make the most of Shipaton! Ready, set, ship! Submissions open on August 1st and close on September 30th. Be sure to carefully review all submission requirements to ensure your app qualifies. We're beyond excited to see what the global builder community creates this year. Register today, and we'll keep you updated via the email address you use there. Let's get shipping! Requirements WHAT TO BUILD Entrants must create a working software application that uses the RevenueCat SDK to power at least one in-app or web purchase (each a "Project"). Apps must be built for iOS, iPadOS, macOS, or Android. The first public version of your app must be released between August 1 and September 30, 2026 . Students competing for the Next Gen Award follow a different, lower-friction path: submit a video and source code instead of a published store listing. No paid Apple or Google developer account required. Students under the age of majority where they reside may enter the Next Gen Award (minimum age 13) with parent or guardian consent. See Section 3 of the official rules. What to submit on Devpost Every submission must include: A text description of your app's features and functionality. A demo video of your project. The video: Should show the app running on the device it was built for. Must be no longer than 2 minutes of essential footage — judges are not required to watch beyond two minutes. Must be uploaded to and publicly visible on YouTube or Vimeo, with the link provided on this form. Must not include third-party trademarks or copyrighted music/material unless you have permission to use it. A URL to your fully published app on the App Store or Google Play or Samsung Galaxy Store. A 1024×1024 app icon . At least one screenshot of the app at 1179px × 2556px with no device frame . Either a free trial in your app, or a promo code so judges can unlock the in-app purchase and test all premium features. the event. Judges want to hear about what you've done post-release to push your app growth to the next level. See official rules for full judging criteria. Best Game Award Open category for the best mobile game shipped during the event. We're looking for great gameplay, art direction, and a monetization fit that suits the genre. See official rules for full judging criteria. RevenueCat Peace Prize Awarded to the project that provides the greatest social good. We're looking for apps with big benefits to communities or society at large. RevenueCat Design Award For the app that best represents the craft of app development, separate from viability as a business. We're looking for innovative ideas and/or beautiful app design and animations. Catvertising Award Celebrates the most creative and effective use of ads as a monetization method. We're looking for clever placements, smart integration with the rest of the revenue stack, and an experience users don't hate. Next Gen Award A student-only category for the best app submitted by active students with a .edu (or equivalent) email address. Judged on a video submission and open-source code — no App Store or Google Play release required. #BuildInPublic Award For developers who shared the most interesting development journey on social media. We're looking for the most compelling lessons learned, or ideas incorporated from feedback from the community. HAMM Award Recognizes the app that makes the smartest use of RevenueCat to drive real revenue. Conflict of Interest Award Awarded to the best overall app submission from employees of RevenueCat or any Shipaton sponsors. Influencer Award — Productivity: Christopher Lawley Build a polished app that helps Apple power users quickly save, organize, and retrieve reusable text, files, documents, and images. Influencer Award — Nutrition & Healthy Eating: Abbey’s Kitchen Create a flexible nutrition app that helps people make meals more satisfying without calorie counting, macro tracking, or restrictive meal plans. Influencer Award — Yoga & Fitness: Simone Sharice Create a personalized wellness companion that turns movement, Pilates, and recovery needs into a clear and achievable plan for today. Influencer Award — Gaming: Mr Lewis Blogs Gaming Build a gaming bucket list where players can easily save, organize, complete, rate, and share the games they want to play. Influencer Award — Career Coaching: Leadership Heather Help new managers practise difficult conversations, receive useful feedback, and build confidence before handling the real situation. Replit’s Idea to Income Use Replit to turn a new idea into a live, monetizing mobile app with growing revenue, returning customers, strong design, and real community interest. Best App for Galaxy — Samsung Publish a high-quality app on the Galaxy Store and make it shine on Samsung devices through thoughtful optimization, features, and foldable support. Most Viral App — Noise Use Noise to create engaging, repeatable content that captures attention, communicates your app’s value, and converts viewers into users. Ship Kotlin Everywhere — JetBrains Build a polished app for iOS and Android with Kotlin Multiplatform or Compose Multiplatform, delivering a consistent, high-quality experience on both platforms. Keep Them Coming Back Award — OneSignal Use OneSignal to create thoughtful notifications, campaigns, or Journeys that improve the experience and give users a meaningful reason to return. The Growth Loop Award — Layers Use Layers to test a focused growth idea, measure the response, explain what you learned, and show how those insights will shape your next experiment. Funnel Vision Award — Stripe Launch a polished web payment funnel with RevenueCat Funnels and Stripe that works reliably, converts users, and processes real payment volume. Questions? Camera. Code. Calling all ecosystem architects and autonomous builders! Step onto the studio lot and transform real-world enterprise chaos into a seamless cinematic production with Gemini. Join Google Cloud and our elite, star-studded partner ecosystem for a first-of-its-kind Summer Blockbuster hackathon! In the era of Agentic AI, writing raw lines of code is just the background noise. The real magic happens when you orchestrate the system. Whether you want to play the visionary Director building production-ready autonomous agent networks, the Technical Producer connecting secure data pipelines via managed MCP servers, or the Studio Head enforcing Cloud IAM security and governance across multi-agent workflows—the backlot is yours. Vibe code with Gemini Enterprise and our leading partner technologies to cast the perfect enterprise tech stack and build the next generation of AI applications fit for the big screen. 🌟 Why Join? Direct Your AI Crew: Get hands-on with Gemini Enterprise Agent Platform and cutting-edge partner tools to transition your local ideas into production-scale architectures. Walk the Red Carpet: Pitch your automated production workflows directly to executive judges, enterprise experts, and elite engineering leaders. 🏆 The Box Office Prizes There are three identical prize buckets—one for each of our featured partner tracks. Instead of a single, crowded pool, you are competing directly within the specific "studio track" of your chosen partner technology. How to Secure the Greenlight: Cast Your Co-Star: Choose the partner platform that holds the data or application workflows your agent needs to interact with. Build with Gemini Enterprise: Build your agentic workflow on Google Cloud using the Gemini Enterprise Agent Platform . Connect to your partner tool using robust enterprise pipelines, API frameworks, or managed protocol adapters. Dominate Your Track: Show off a deterministic, multi-step agent that solves enterprise friction. You will be judged exclusively against other builders inside your chosen partner track. Requirements What to Build 🎬 Build a functional agent—powered by Gemini and Google Cloud Agent Builder—that integrates a Partner Entity's product or MCP to power a real media & entertainment workflow. Partners: IBM Grafana Labs Parallel Clickhouse Replit Check out the full hackathon resources here . 📋 Submission Requirements Include a URL to the hosted Project The 3-Minute Trailer (Demo Video): a demo video showing your project/agent functioning as built — not a cinematic trailer. Upload to YouTube or Vimeo, make it publicly visible, and make sure it's in English or includes English subtitles. Include a URL to your open-source code repository for judging and testing on either GitHub, GitLab or Bitbucket. It must contain all source code, assets, and instructions needed to run, and must demonstrate actual runtime use of Google Cloud and your chosen Partner's service (imported and called in code, not just named in the README) The repository must be public and include a complete open source license file. This license should be detectable and visible at the top of the repository page (in the About section) Select which partner track you'll be submitting to Your completed Devpost submission form Read the full Official Rules for detailed partner track requirements and eligibility terms Hackathon Sponsors Prizes $ 75,000 in prizes IBM - 1st Place $ 7,500 in cash 1 winner Opportunity for a social media promotion IBM - 2nd Place $ 4,500 in cash 1 winner IBM - 3rd Place $ 3,000 in cash 1 winner Grafana Labs - 1st Place $ 7,500 in cash 1 winner Opportunity for a social media promotion Grafana Labs - 2nd Place $ 4,500 in cash 1 winner Grafana Labs - 3rd Place $ 3,000 in cash 1 winner Parallel - 1st Place $ 7,500 in cash 1 winner Opportunity for a social media promotion Parallel - 2nd Place $ 4,500 in cash 1 winner Parallel - 3rd Place $ 3,000 in cash 1 winner Clickhouse - 1st Place $ 7,500 in cash 1 winner Opportunity for a social media promotion Clickhouse - 2nd Place $ 4,500 in cash 1 winner Clickhouse - 3rd Place $ 3,000 in cash 1 winner Replit - 1st Place $ 7,500 in cash 1 winner Opportunity for a social media promotion Replit - 2nd Place $ 4,500 in cash 1 winner Replit - 3rd Place $ 3,000 in cash 1 winner Devpost Achievements Submitting to this hackathon could earn you:

Build with Gemini Enterprise: Build your agentic workflow on Google Cloud using the Gemini Enterprise Agent Platform . Dominate Your Track: Show off a deterministic, multi-step agent that solves enterprise friction. You will be judged exclusively against other builders inside your chosen partner track.
